entries.purpose: Colab notebook standard: required cells, structure, vocabulary rules, validation checklist for every jaxfne tutorial notebook.
entries.evidence: Re-checked the flagged claim directly: `python3 -c "import jaxfne as jtfne; print(hasattr(jtfne.Model, 'simulate'))"` -> True. Read jaxfne/core.py: Model.simulate is a real instance method (core.py:4560-...), and jtfne.simulate (core.py:6836) is a free function that is a thin wrapper literally calling `model.simulate(sim, paradigm=paradigm)` internally (core.py:6873). Built and ran a real minimal example (laminar_cortex_config -> construct -> both model.simulate(sim) and jtfne.simulate(model, sim)): both executed successfully, returned jaxfne.core.Signals, and model.manifest(signals) worked. So the prior review's premise ('model.simulate(sim) genuinely doesn't work') was FALSE -- both call shapes are real and equivalent. Still edited docs/tutorials/notebook_standard.md section 6 (line ~53) to use jtfne.simulate(model, sim) instead of model.simulate(sim), purely for consistency with docs/tutorials/13_canonical_column_etude.md and docs/tutorials/index.md (both use the free-function form), with an inline comment noting the two are equivalent -- not because the old code was broken.
entries.review_reverification_note: Re-run 2026-07-05: `hasattr(jtfne.Model,'simulate')` -> True, `hasattr(jtfne,'simulate')` -> True -- both call shapes still real and equivalent.
